questions.prompt: Opening and closing a door produce the same set of frames in reverse order. A model that averages per-frame features and classifies the average will
options: succeed because the frames are the same
be at chance on the pair
questions.explanation: The average is identical for both, so the label cannot be a function of it.

questions.prompt: Which is a likely cause of inflated test accuracy on a video benchmark?
options: Reporting accuracy per clip instead of per frame in the test set.
Using a lower frame rate when the frames are sampled for testing.
Using a larger test set than the one used in the training split.
Frames from the same clip appear in both training and test splits.
questions.explanation: Neighbouring frames are almost identical, so the split must be by clip, actor or scene.

questions.prompt: A SlowFast network gives the fast pathway fewer channels than the slow one. Why is that reasonable?
options: Fast pathways cannot have many channels because they run at a high frame rate.
Appearance needs a high frame rate, so the slow path should have fewer channels.
Motion needs fine temporal sampling but little spatial detail; appearance changes slowly.
It reduces aliasing in the slow pathway by removing most of its channels.
questions.explanation: Each path specialises: slow for appearance, fast for motion.
